label: Rough Trade Records
release_notes: Fourth album from the Dublin noise-rock band (formerly Girl Band) and the first since Most Normal (2022). Dara Kiely - vocals; Alan Duggan Borges - guitar; Daniel Fox - bass; Adam Faulkner - drums. No guests are credited.
Recorded 2022 to 2026 at Hellfire, Yellow Door Music Studio and Sonic Studios in Dublin. Produced by Gilla Band; recorded and mixed by bassist Daniel Fox. No mastering credit found.
Between albums: Kiely took up painting, Borges launched the solo project Null Club, Fox produced Sprints, Lambrini Girls and Mandy, Indiana, and Faulkner toured on drums with Lankum.
Singles: Giraffe (May 27, 2026, also a limited picture-disc 7-inch), Placeholder (July 7, with the album announcement) and Alogia (Sept. 8, video directed by Cuan Roche).

Paste ties the record to Kiely's grief over his estranged father's death in late 2022. Alogia was written after a schizophrenia diagnosis (Kiely, via Northern Transmissions). Paste and Quietus both note a PĒRKONS HD-01 drum machine at the core of the sound.

10 tracks, 42:16. Out Sept. 25, 2026. Metacritic 85/100 (15 critics); Pitchfork 8.8 and Best New Music; The Guardian 5 stars; Mojo less favorable (per Wikipedia). Charted No. 34 in Ireland and No. 15 on the UK Independent Albums chart.

pull_quotes.text: Dublin rock band deliver their most punishing record to date
four people going feral in a rage room

draft_comment: Abrasive, industrial-flecked noise rock and post-punk from Dublin, their first album in four years. Critics call it their most punishing yet, and too bad six of the ten tracks are FCC.

tracks.notes: Second single (July 7, 2026), released with the album announcement. Kiely says it is about comfort distractions and childhood nostalgia (via The Line of Best Fit).

tracks.title: Alogia
tracks.notes: Third single (Sept. 8, 2026), video directed by Cuan Roche. The title means poverty of speech; written after Kiely's schizophrenia diagnosis.

tracks.notes: Paste describes screeching, stuttering synths and a Power Rangers theme.

tracks.title: At the Gallop
tracks.notes: Closer. Named for the 1975 debut album by Cromwell, the prog band of Kiely's late father (Paste, The Quietus). Vocoder-processed vocal. Listed as "The Gallop" on pre-release tracklists.
